collection_method.banking-events: Fineract's external-events Kafka topic, read on the VM between broker offsets taken before the window opened and the topic's end after it closed; each message decoded with the pinned Avro schemas and kept if its createdAt falls inside the window
collection_method.banking-audit: m_portfolio_command_source (Fineract's command audit trail) queried on the VM for rows whose made_on_date_utc falls inside the window, joined to m_appuser for the maker's and checker's logins

scenario.attacker_credential: phished before the window; used, not simulated

timestamps.banking-events: event.createdAt is UTC in ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME — no zone suffix, as Fineract writes it. It agrees with the staging table's created_at and with the audit trail's made_on_date_utc to within milliseconds. kafka.timestamp_ms is when the publish job sent it, which is later and is NOT when the transaction happened
timestamps.banking-audit: made_on_date_utc is a timestamptz rendered with +00:00. made_on_date, the tenant-local column, is empty on this build
timestamps.business_date: a tenant-local calendar date (tenant timezone Asia/Kolkata), so near midnight UTC it can name a different day. It is Fineract's accounting date, not a timestamp

bank_minus_lab_seconds.note: made_on_date_utc (bank clock) minus sent_at (lab clock); includes request latency, so it is an upper bound on clock skew

completeness.banking-audit: 5 of 5 operations that change something have their audit row
completeness.banking-events: 5 of 5 operations that change something have all their events (10 of 10 events)
completeness.reads: 10 reads (balance checks, statements) change nothing, so the bank records nothing for them; they appear only in the network sources

bank_minus_lab_seconds.note: made_on_date_utc (bank clock) minus sent_at (lab clock); includes request latency, so it is an upper bound on clock skew

banking-events_20260930231144.raw.jsonl.role: the broker's own bytes for every message read; not submitted — kept so the decode can be checked

banking_20260930231144.groundtruth.json.role: labels, known before sending; never submitted

caveats: the bank's audit trail attributes every command to a login (maker_username), not an address: m_portfolio_command_source.client_ip exists on this build but was empty for all 5 rows. Even filled, it would show the tunnel's end on the VM rather than the namespace address, as a production bank behind a proxy or load balancer would. The actor's network identity comes from this window's firewall and IDS items, joined by time

the loan officer holds Fineract's stock 'Super user' role, so one phished login could both approve and disburse. A bank would split those between people; the missing second approver (checker_username null) is the finding. Customers hold a restricted 'PDE Customer' role: they can apply for a loan but are refused approving one (HTTP 403, checked when seeding), which is why the fraud needs the officer's credential at all

customers bank through Fineract's standard API with their own logins, not a self-service API: this build (1.16.0-SNAPSHOT) has none. Nothing in the standard API stops a customer's login from reading or moving another customer's money; a real bank's online-banking layer would enforce that. Every customer action is still attributed to that customer's own login
the attacker's use of the officer's credential is simulated; the phishing that obtained it is not, and happened before the window
the publish job ('Send Asynchronous Events') was triggered at collection time rather than waited for on its one-minute tick. That moves when events were sent, never their createdAt

a transfer publishes two events — a withdrawal on the payer's account and a deposit on the payee's — neither carrying the transfer's id, so both are matched by account and amount. A disbursal also raises its transaction event, which appears in completeness.detail as unexplained — expected, and listed so the counts reconcile

any audit row or event inside the window that the scenario did not cause is listed under unexplained, not removed: the publish job writes its own EXECUTEJOB row, and anyone else using the bank in the window would appear too
the collector redacts credential-bearing fields in command_as_json (a user-creation command stores the new password) and marks the row collector_redacted; 0 row(s) this window

the mule is a seeded customer (externalId pde-mule) and applies again in every fraud window, so earlier windows' loans to the same client exist; this window's is the one with the resource_id recorded in the ground truth
both artifacts were hashed on the VM before leaving it and verified here after transfer; the digests above are those, and are what the EvidenceItems should carry
